summary: Observations of firework flashes.
description: On December 31, 1977, after 7:00 PM, several people observed an intriguing orange light in the sky. A neighbor, having learned of these events reported in the press, came forward to give a statement to the police. He claimed to have set off a fireworks display consisting of two flares and four Chinese rockets on December 31 between 7:00 and 7:30 PM to celebrate the New Year. Another witness reported an observation around 5:00 PM on December 31, 1977. A motorist spotted a stationary object in the sky, which quickly disappeared from sight. This testimony was brief, and no other accounts of the phenomenon provided further information.

summary: Periodic observations of a luminous object: lack of information.
description: Periodic sightings of a luminous object have been reported. These occurred on December 19th around 10 PM and on December 20th at 4 AM and again around 10 PM. Witnesses observed a luminous object for extended periods each time, emitting alternating green, orange, and then red lights. The object moved, making distinct stops. During the police investigation, television interference was noted at the times the object was observed in the early evening. The possibility of observation by a communications satellite was raised but not confirmed due to a lack of information.

summary: Observation in the sky of a luminous phenomenon in the shape of a ball whose upper part is flat: misinterpretation of a gibbous moon.
description: On December 19, 1977, at approximately 2:00 AM, a motorist driving on the D109 observed a luminous phenomenon in the sky. The UAP (Unidentified Aerial Phenomenon), shaped like a sphere with a flat top, emitted a white glow and appeared to be stationary above a valley. The witness decided to investigate and observed the UAP moving at a moderate speed westward. He followed the UAP for about thirty minutes without ever catching up with it. No other reports of this phenomenon were collected by the gendarmerie. This sighting, formerly known as Arinthod (39) after the gendarmerie, is classified as a "C" case due to a lack of information and is currently being re-examined (see the Investigation Notes document). This case is quite consistent (a witness, accompanied by a dog that reacted to the presence of the UFO), and the description of the observed UFO is quite precise. The witness's sincerity and credibility have never been questioned. The described phenomenon shares many characteristics (duration of observation, shape, size, color) with a well-known astronomical object: the Moon at sunset. Furthermore, the Moon was indeed present in the observed area of the sky, even though the witness did not mention it. It is not the witness's visual perception that is at issue, but rather the witness's interpretation of the observation based on their feelings (fatigue, night driving). In the current GEIPAN classification, this case of moderate strangeness is classified as "A": observation linked to a misidentification of the gibbous Moon.

summary: Multiple observations of a red-orange phenomenon in the sky and disappearance in the West: mistaken for the Moon at sunset.
description: On December 18, 1977, at approximately 1:20 a.m., about ten people in a hamlet in the commune of Sainte-Cerotte (72) observed a red-orange phenomenon in the sky. The witnesses could not estimate the distance to the phenomenon and disagreed on its shape. However, all noted the object's movements (descent and ascent) and its gradual disappearance towards the west. No unusual noises were heard during the observation of this phenomenon, and no other witness statements were collected by the gendarmerie. This observation is classified as a C case by GEPAN under the name SAINT-CALAIS (72) 12/18/1977. It was recently re-examined (see the document "Investigation Notes"). This case is consistent (approximately ten witnesses), and the description of the observed UFO is quite precise. The sincerity and credibility of the witnesses have never been questioned. The described phenomenon shares many characteristics (duration of observation, shape, size, color) with a well-known astronomical object: the Moon at sunset. Furthermore, the Moon was indeed present in the observed area of the sky, even though the witnesses did not mention it. The issue is not the witnesses' visual perception, but rather their interpretation of the observation based on their own experience (fatigue, nighttime observation, misinterpretation of the Moon's position). In the current GEIPAN classification, this case of moderate strangeness is categorized as "A," indicating an observation linked to a misidentification of the Moon.

summary: Probable observations of atmospheric reentry.
description: On December 17, 1977, around midnight, several members of the same family observed a luminous phenomenon for a few seconds on their doorsteps. A yellow-orange sphere moved from the northeast to the south at very high speed. It left behind a glow that illuminated the night. These people likely witnessed an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Probable observations of atmospheric reentry.
description: On December 13, 1977, between 7:00 and 7:30 PM, several witnesses in different regions of France observed a circular luminous phenomenon rapidly moving east to west across the sky, followed by a trail. Most of these observations lasted only a few seconds, and no unusual noises were heard. Based on the descriptions provided, these individuals likely witnessed an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Observation of the passage of a luminous phenomenon.
description: On December 7, 1977, at approximately 6:45 PM, several people observed a luminous phenomenon in the sky. It moved from west to east without any unusual noise being heard. The phenomenon appeared as an elongated shape emitting a white light. As it moved, this shape transformed into a red point of light that gradually faded and disappeared. During the investigation, the gendarmerie found no trace of the phenomenon on the ground. A witness reported also seeing an orange ball in the sky on December 4 at approximately 10:15 PM. While these accounts resemble descriptions of atmospheric reentry observations, the information concerning these phenomena remains too imprecise to validate this hypothesis.

summary: Observation of an object delimited by lights.
description: On November 30, 1977, at approximately 5:35 PM, a motorist repeatedly observed a luminous phenomenon along his route. It consisted of two very bright white spheres, between which numerous points of light appeared to define a device. It moved at varying altitudes and changed direction without any unusual noise being heard. No flashing was observed in the lights. The witness noticed no interference on the radio or in the vehicle and then lost sight of the phenomenon. No other witness statements were collected.

summary: Observation of a luminous phenomenon.
description: On November 26, 1977, at approximately 6:30 p.m., a driver and his passenger observed a luminous phenomenon that intrigued them. Throughout their journey, the phenomenon was visible, changing shape but maintaining its reddish-orange color. It did not appear to move. No other accounts were collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack further details.

summary: Observation of the passage of an oval object. Change of direction.
description: On November 24, 1977, at 7:20 a.m., a witness observed an oval-shaped object, about the size of a rugby ball. It emitted a bright light and moved along an east-north trajectory before turning around, traveling back the same distance, and disappearing into the urban landscape. The observation lasted approximately thirty seconds, during which no unusual noise was heard. No other accounts of this phenomenon were collected, and we lack further information about it.

summary: Probable observation of an electrical phenomenon.
description: On November 19, 1977, at approximately 1:05 AM, a driver and his passenger spotted a reddish-orange sphere moving and approaching. The driver stopped, and the object remained motionless in a meadow, 1.5 meters above the ground and about 30 meters from the car. No sound was heard. The frightened driver decided to continue his journey and change his route, but he encountered the phenomenon several times during his travels. The phenomenon was seen for fifteen minutes and over nine kilometers by the drivers before disappearing. No traces or clues were found at the various locations where the phenomenon was observed. No unusual activity was noted by the head of the Floirac observatory. No military operations were conducted that night. No work of any kind was carried out on the high-voltage power line or transformers located near the roads traveled by the driver. Nevertheless, it is likely that the observed manifestation can be attributed to an electrical phenomenon, given that it was seen progressing always in the vicinity of materials conducting and transforming electricity.

summary: Probable observations of atmospheric reentry.
description: On November 15, 1977, at approximately 6:45 a.m., a witness on a moped suddenly spotted an elongated object in the sky, moving rapidly to the northwest. Moments later, the witness observed the object burst into a shower of sparks that fell to the ground, revealing a multicolored sphere that continued in the same direction before disappearing completely. No unusual noises were heard during the observation. Another witness at the same time saw a luminous phenomenon followed by a long, multicolored trail. The gendarmerie found no trace of it on the ground in the area. No other reports were collected regarding this phenomenon. These witnesses likely witnessed an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Probable sighting of a weather balloon.
description: On November 12, 1977, at approximately 4:53 PM, two people observed a luminous, elongated object in the sky. It appeared to be stationary at first, then gradually rose into the air before disappearing instantly into the clouds. No unusual noises were heard during the observation, which lasted more than twenty seconds. No particular military maneuvers were carried out at the military camp that day. These witnesses likely observed the passage of a weather balloon illuminated by the setting sun.

summary: Probable sighting of a weather balloon.
description: On November 10, 1977, at 7:15 a.m., two people from their homes noticed a stationary point of light in the sky, which intrigued them. Around 7:35 a.m., the object began to move, and the witnesses observed a grayish, oblong, perfectly smooth object followed by a rapidly disappearing plume. The object's speed increased, and it quickly disappeared behind a hill around 7:40 a.m. No noise was heard during the entire observation. No particular observations were made at the airbase control tower or the Dijon-Longvic weather station, where visibility conditions at the time were rather poor. An additional witness was found, but was unable to provide significant details about the observed phenomenon. Based on the serious description given by the main witness, these people probably observed a weather balloon.

summary: Observing a kite.
description: On November 10, 1977, around 7:00 PM, witnesses in a restaurant in Kourou observed a luminous object performing geometric figures in the sky for about fifteen minutes. It disappeared, descending in a spiral. No aircraft movements, balloon launches, or weather rockets were reported that day. A witness came forward to the police station on November 11, 1977, to report that the previous day, around the time of the aforementioned events, he had seen a battery-powered kite land in the parking lot of a hotel in the town. Despite searches, the kite's owner was not found.

summary: Observation of the passage of a luminous sphere.
description: A witness reported observing a luminous sphere passing from southwest to northeast around 6:15 PM on November 4, 1977. No such phenomenon was observed by the meteorological and radar station at Air Base 105 in Évreux. The regional press reported sightings of this phenomenon by two other people, about which we lack further information.

summary: Observation of the passage of a bright white object.
description: On November 4, 1977, a witness on a bus observed a rapidly moving, ovoid object maintaining its altitude. The object quickly disappeared, hidden by the urban landscape. No information was obtained from the Paris Observatory regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack details.

summary: Probable astronomical observation.
description: The gendarmerie was informed through the press that several people had observed a luminous phenomenon in the sky on multiple occasions. The witnesses' descriptions varied, including whether it was a ball or a glow, its color (white and red), flashing or not, moving or stationary. Air surveillance services at Air Base 105 in Evreux-Fauville did not notice any unusual phenomena in the sky on October 28, 1977. The gendarmerie received no other reports regarding this phenomenon. These individuals were likely making an astronomical observation.

summary: Probable observation of atmospheric reentry.
description: On October 27, 1977, at approximately 6:00 AM, two people briefly glimpsed a red fireball in the sky, followed by a long red and orange trail. This phenomenon moved from east to west at very high speed and disappeared abruptly. No sound was heard. These witnesses likely observed an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Observations of a red luminous phenomenon on the horizon: mistaken for the setting sun.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive. Its publications include older cases, originally classified as type C, which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even an explicit change in classification within an investigation report. This observation is one of the cases classified as type C that have been re-examined (see the Investigation Notes document). On October 24, 1977, between 5:15 p.m. and 6:00 p.m. (times vary depending on the witness), three residents of Guise (02) observed a red or fire-colored sphere on the horizon, from which small flames were emitting. The observation lasted from five to ten minutes, after which the UFO gradually disappeared over the horizon. The witnesses filed statements with the gendarmerie on October 25th and 27th. On patrol for several consecutive days, the gendarmes observed no unusual activity and collected no further testimonies. The case was the subject of a press article published in the newspaper L'Union on October 26, 1977 (see the document "Investigation Notes"). This case is consistent (three witnesses), and the description of the observed UFO is quite precise. The sincerity and credibility of the witnesses have never been questioned. The described phenomenon shares many characteristics (duration of observation, shape, size, color) with a well-known astronomical object: the setting Sun. Indeed, the Sun was setting along the axis indicated by the witnesses. It is not the visual perception of the witnesses that is the issue, but rather their interpretation of their observation through their feelings (astonishment). In the current GEIPAN classification, this case of weak strangeness is classified as UAP A, an observation linked to a misinterpretation of the setting sun.

summary: Observation of the passage of a flashing luminous ball.
description: On October 21, 1977, at approximately 6:30 PM, a witness observed a luminous phenomenon for a few seconds. A flashing yellow sphere moved along a west-east trajectory. No trail or sound was observed. The police investigation yielded no other reports of this phenomenon. Particularly stormy weather with numerous lightning strikes affected the entire region that day.

summary: Observation of the passage of an elongated object.
description: On October 21, 1977, at approximately 5:15 PM, two witnesses observed an elongated object moving across the sky. Luminous and multicolored, the object moved, leaving behind a fading glow. It quickly disappeared, hidden by the landscape. No further accounts of this phenomenon were collected, and information about it remains scarce.

summary: Rapid movement of a luminous phenomenon across the sky.
description: On October 21, 1977, at approximately 6:30 PM, two people observed a luminous, round object moving horizontally eastward. The object quickly disappeared into the cloud cover. No sound was heard. No further reports were collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Observation of the movement of an unknown object.
description: On October 18, 1977, at 12:24 a.m., a witness observed a bright point in the sky for four minutes. The object approached, traced a wide arc as it lost altitude, and appeared to hover above a hill. The witness recounted seeing the dark mass of a craft with a circular porthole emitting a bright blue and orange light. After ten seconds, it vanished instantly. Despite a police investigation, no other witness statements were collected.

summary: Observing the movement of a bright object in the sky.
description: On October 16, 1977, at 6:00 AM, a witness observed a bright object moving from left to right from their balcony. It rapidly gained altitude and disappeared into the sky. No other accounts of this phenomenon were collected, and information about it remains scarce.

summary: Observation of the passage of a circular object: curvilinear trajectory.
description: On October 16, 1977, at approximately 3:30 a.m., a driver and his passenger observed a colored, circular object passing overhead. The object traveled at high altitude and high speed. Its trajectory was curvilinear, and it disappeared behind vegetation. No signs of interference were observed in the vehicle. No other reports of this phenomenon were collected.

summary: Probable observation of an optical effect related to the rising sun.
description: On October 12, 1977, at 5:45 a.m., a motorist observed an object in the sky surrounded by an orange halo, vibrating or oscillating. No other reports of this phenomenon were collected by the gendarmerie or the Floirac Observatory (33). Although the account was very brief, this person likely observed the rising sun (which rose at 5:20 a.m. that day) through a cloud.

summary: Observations of luminous phenomena.
description: On October 9, 1977, from 8:30 p.m. to 11:30 p.m., several people, including gendarmes, observed a luminous phenomenon with varying colors, unlike the stars. Another luminous phenomenon was observed later that same day around 9:00 p.m. by a witness. This witness reported seeing two intensely white and symmetrical beams of light on the ground. A third observation was reported on October 12, 1977, at 7:45 p.m.: a witness observed a phenomenon illuminating its entire surroundings for two seconds, consisting of beams of light in various colors, like a firework display. The gendarmerie investigation did not establish a connection between the observations, for which we lack further information.

summary: Observation of the passage of a luminous object with a phosphorescent trail.
description: On October 9, 1977, at approximately 7:15 PM, two soldiers on duty observed an oval-shaped object moving in the sky from north-south. The object ascended and descended slowly, leaving a phosphorescent trail behind it. No noise was heard during the observation, which lasted between 5 and 7 minutes. A similar observation had been reported a few years earlier: at that time, it involved weather balloons launched from the Istres airbase (13).

summary: Probable sighting of an aircraft.
description: On October 8, 1977, between 12:30 a.m. and 1:00 a.m., a person on a moped observed an unfamiliar object. It had a flat base topped with a rounded shape; the object was entirely illuminated at its base by yellow lights surrounding a larger red light in the center. The frightened witness reported being followed for three kilometers to his home. The object then stopped above his house before speeding off again. The description of the lights suggests that this witness likely observed a helicopter-type aircraft.

summary: Observation of an orange luminous phenomenon seemingly following motorists: astronomical observation of the Moon.
description: On October 2, 1977, between 9:50 PM and 10:00 PM, motorists in two different areas of the Sarthe department observed a luminous phenomenon in the sky that they could not explain. The object was round, slightly flattened on top, and orange in color. This case was initially classified as C by SEPRA due to a lack of information, then re-analyzed in 2013 by an internet user who proposed an explanation to GEIPAN, which was subsequently validated. This observation is a typical case of a "following ball" phenomenon: an effect observed when witnesses see a point or disc of light that seems to accompany them as they move. In fact, this very distant object is always in the same geographical direction, and it is generally a celestial body. The testimony is very consistent, with two independent groups of witnesses who filed their statements with the gendarmerie. The observed phenomenon is not very strange, as it strongly resembles the moon. GEIPAN classifies this case as A: observation of the Moon.

summary: Observation of a luminous sphere passing by. Glow on the ground.
description: On October 2, 1977, late in the day, a farmer working in a field was briefly overflown by a luminous spherical object. Other people observed an unusual glow at the far end of the field where the farmer was standing. The police, notified three days later, found no trace on the ground in the area indicated by the witnesses, and no further witness statements were collected that could provide more details.

summary: Probable sightings of aircraft in a holding pattern for landing.
description: On the evening of September 30, 1977, many people observed objects in the sky moving very slowly at high altitude and emitting flashing colored lights. The events occurred over the city of Sens and in the Brienon-sur-Armançon area of the Yonne department. It is likely that the observed phenomenon was due to significant and unusual air traffic in the region, and to the activation of the holding pattern at Sens airport.

summary: Observation of the passage of two vehicles.
description: On September 23, 1977, around midnight, a person walking their dog spotted two circular objects in the sky for about a minute. Their undersides were bright white, while their upper surfaces were darker. The objects moved silently from northwest to southeast. They began to turn before gaining altitude at high speed and disappearing. No unexpected echoes were detected during the night at the control tower of the Istres air base. No other reports were collected.

summary: Observation of the movement of a luminous phenomenon.
description: Following a press article reporting three witnesses' sightings of a "UFO," an investigation was opened. The gendarmerie located one witness who stated that on September 13, 1977, around 9:30 PM, she observed a reddish glow moving north-south. No noise was heard during the sighting. No trail was observed in its wake. The second witness remains untraceable. A third witness was interviewed but stated that he observed a luminous, white, oval object in the clouds on September 7, 1977, around 7:00 AM. No further testimonies concerning the September 13th phenomenon were collected.

summary: Observations of a red-orange phenomenon in the sky.
description: On September 5, 1977, between 10:30 PM and 11:15 PM, three people observed an unusual phenomenon in the sky for several minutes. All witnesses described the movements of a luminous red-orange sphere which, according to them, remained stationary or moved from right to left and up and down before taking a downward trajectory and disappearing. No trace of it was found on the ground in the area. This phenomenon appears to have followed a NE-W trajectory. Too few details were provided to validate any particular hypothesis. This case is classified as Class C due to lack of information.

summary: Observation of a luminous object passing by. No noise.
description: On September 4, 1977, around 11:00 PM, two people observed an unusual phenomenon in the sky. A very bright white ball moved at high speed. It disappeared from the witnesses' sight as it moved away. No sound was heard during the observation, which lasted only a few seconds. The police were unable to make any findings regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Probable sighting of an aircraft.
description: According to a letter received by the gendarmerie, a witness on vacation reportedly saw three slightly flattened, egg-shaped objects moving on September 1, 1977, at 8:15 PM. They were shiny and emitted beams of light. No other witness statements were collected in the area where the sighting took place, an area regularly overflown by aircraft from two nearby airfields. The witness likely reported seeing an aircraft.

summary: Observations of a stationary and silent luminous object.
description: On August 26, 1977, at approximately 8:15 PM, several people observed a motionless and silent luminous object between two trees. The phenomenon was observed through binoculars before suddenly disappearing.

summary: Observation of the movement of a luminous sphere.
description: Following a local newspaper article, two witnesses were interviewed about their observation on August 15, 1977, at approximately 12:05 a.m., of a luminous, spherical object coming from the southwest. It moved slowly at a low altitude, stopped for a few seconds, and then moved northeast at a higher speed. No sound was heard during the observation, which lasted several minutes. No other accounts were collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Observation of a luminous phenomenon. Disappearance at very high speed.
description: On August 12, 1977, at approximately 11:00 PM, a witness observed a thin, elongated, stationary, and very bright object in the sky. This phenomenon disappeared at high speed in the southwest direction after a few seconds. No other accounts were collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Probable sighting of an aircraft.
description: Following a local newspaper report indicating that a witness had seen an unidentified flying object in the sky, the gendarmerie began searching for other potential witnesses. Two witnesses were located, stating that they observed a very bright, stationary object in the sky around 10:30 PM on August 11, 1977. Observed through binoculars, the object had spheres emitting a yellow light at its base and a sort of flashing red light. It then moved slowly without any sound before disappearing. These witnesses likely observed the passage of a helicopter-type aircraft.

summary: Observation of a luminous orange and triangular phenomenon: lack of information
description: The gendarmerie was alerted to a sighting reported in the local press. On August 7, 1977, around 1:30 a.m., several people observed a bright point of light at the top of a hill, which then gradually became a large, bright orange triangle. When viewed in its entirety, the object was shaped like a donkey and appeared to be moving towards them. Frightened, the witnesses left in their cars. The phenomenon disappeared, hidden behind a hedge of trees. Returning to the site a little later with other people, they observed nothing further. At the location indicated by the witnesses, the gendarmerie found no traces on the ground, and no other statements were collected from the local population.

summary: Observation of the movement of a luminous phenomenon.
description: On August 6, 1977, at 1:30 a.m., two people outside their home observed a mysterious luminous phenomenon. A bright yellow-orange glow moved slowly, stopped, and the witnesses briefly glimpsed two small red lights before the glow continued on its path. No noise was heard during the three minutes of observation. On August 13, 1977, at the same time, one of the witnesses again observed, from his home, an ovoid object in a field on the other side of the river bordering his property. The luminous object was stationary on the ground, and no noise was heard during the ten minutes of observation. The field owner noticed no unusual marks or changes at the presumed location of the object. The police found three shallow holes but were unable to determine their exact origin. Soil samples will be taken. Tests for radioactivity will be negative, as will the verifications requested from the meteorological, engineering, and nearby radar services. No further witness statements will be collected regarding this phenomenon.

summary: Observations of luminous phenomena.
description: On September 18, 1977, between 10:30 and 10:35 PM, two witnesses observed a bright orange-orange luminous phenomenon moving from north-northeast to south-southwest. The witnesses had time to see a rectangular shape that quickly disappeared behind a hill. A third witness stated that he saw nothing that day, but that three weeks earlier he had seen a bright light behind another hill. No other reports were collected, and no trace was found in the areas where these phenomena were thought to have disappeared, leaving us with no information.

summary: Observations of three stationary and bright craft.
description: On July 27, 1977, at 3:55 a.m., members of the same family observed three objects hovering below the cloud ceiling for one to two minutes. They described the objects as having a flared, pyramidal shape with a rounded top. They emitted a white and colored light of varying intensity. They disappeared silently and in a few seconds around 4:00 a.m., reappearing around 4:20 a.m. They then vanished completely into the clouds. No official report was made by the gendarmerie, and no other witness statements were collected.

summary: Sighting of a saucer-shaped craft.
description: person testified in a letter that on July 20, 1977, at approximately 1:00 AM, while in their car, they and their daughter observed a saucer-shaped object for a few seconds. Surrounded by a slightly yellow halo, the object moved slowly across the sky, rotating, and appeared to descend toward the car. However, as it gained altitude, the object disappeared in the direction of Bordeaux. Several people were interviewed, but no other testimonies were collected to confirm or refute this witness's account.

summary: Observation of a sphere and luminous discs.
description: On July 19, 1977, around 11:00 PM, a hunter in the forest observed a multicolored luminous sphere moving in the sky. Continuing his search towards the edge of the forest, he spotted, in the same spot where the luminous sphere had disappeared, pale colored discs about the size of a dinner plate. The bewildered hunter went to a chalet to find someone who could confirm what he was seeing. Another witness confirmed to the police that he had seen three stationary luminous discs in the sky through binoculars. Around midnight, no objects were visible in the sky. No other testimonies that could provide further information about this phenomenon have been collected.

summary: Observation of a luminous phenomenon.
description: The gendarmerie reports letters describing a luminous phenomenon observed on July 2, 1977, by two people. A couple observed, between 7:30 p.m. and 8:20 p.m., two yellow-orange lights that were initially stationary and then moved across the sky. One of the lights disappeared instantly, and the witnesses left their observation point before the second light vanished. The witnesses never responded to the gendarmerie's summons, and no further testimonies were collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Observations of a luminous phenomenon.
description: On June 25, 1977, at 2:05 a.m., the police were alerted to the presence of unusual light phenomena in the sky. Witnesses reported seeing two beams of light moving between 1:05 a.m. and 2:05 a.m. These beams moved across the sky, illuminating the area as they rotated. The light appeared every 15 to 20 seconds. Arriving at the scene at 2:30 a.m., the police found no evidence of any such phenomenon.

summary: Probable atmospheric re-entry.
description: On June 13, 1977, at approximately 12:05 a.m., motorists noticed the road light up as if in broad daylight for four to five seconds. They saw a ball followed by a trail moving from west to east. This ball emitted a crackling sound. It quickly disappeared, hidden by the landscape. Other witnesses in the vicinity heard a loud bang or saw a flash. The gendarmerie found no evidence of a fall in the area. These people likely witnessed an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Observation of a dark, stationary point.
description: On June 4, 1977, at approximately 11:00 AM, a witness and his son observed a small, dark-colored point of light against the clear sky. This point remained stationary, and during the observation, flashes of various colors were noted. No sound was heard. No other accounts of this phenomenon were collected, and information about it remains scarce.

summary: Observation of the presence of a luminous red-orange ball in the sky: astronomical observation with misinterpretation of the Moon.
description: On May 30, 1977, at 3:30 a.m., two people in a car observed a luminous red-orange sphere above the town of Vitteaux. This sphere was at low altitude and moved slowly from south to north. No noise was heard during the observation, which lasted 5 to 6 minutes. This old case has been re-examined. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience acquired over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even an explicit change in classification in an investigation report. This case is consistent (two witnesses, including a police officer), and the description of the observed UFO is very precise. The sincerity and credibility of the witnesses have never been questioned. The described phenomenon shares many characteristics (duration of observation, shape, size, color) with a well-known astronomical object: the Moon at sunset. Furthermore, the Moon was clearly visible in the observed area of the sky, even though the witnesses did not mention it. The issue is not the witnesses' visual perception, but rather their interpretation of the observation based on their own experience (fatigue, night driving, the Moon seen intermittently through clouds). In the current GEIPAN classification, this case of a weak anomaly is classified as UAP A, an observation linked to a misidentification of the Moon.

summary: Probable astronomical observation of the Moon.
description: On May 28, 1977, starting at 3:00 AM, a student made three observations of a luminous phenomenon that intrigued her. A yellow ball moved slowly before disappearing. No sound was heard during the observation. Another witness came to the observation site the following day between 2:00 and 4:00 AM. Directly above the observation point indicated by the first witness, he noted the presence of the Moon. The student had likely made an astronomical observation of the Moon.

summary: Observations of a ballet of a luminous phenomenon.
description: On May 13, 1977, at approximately 9:30 PM, several witnesses observed the movement of several luminous points. These points changed color over a considerable distance, which the witnesses could not estimate more precisely. This series of movements continued until 10:20 PM, when the phenomenon abruptly disappeared.

summary: Observation of two orange balls emitting light.
description: On May 11, 1977, at approximately 11:20 PM, a person noticed two enormous luminous spheres located to the east of their house. Approximately 50 meters above the ground, they were motionless and brightly illuminated the ground. About a minute later, before the phenomenon completely disappeared, the witness heard a sound like helicopter blades and saw a very intense yellow light illuminate the area. No other accounts of this phenomenon were collected, and we lack further information about it.

summary: Observations of a night flight of helicopters.
description: On May 11, 1977, between 10:05 PM and 10:25 PM, several people observed two objects in the sky moving silently and emitting a bright red glow intermittently. Witnesses also noted that these objects emitted a white glow towards the ground. The gendarmerie investigation determined that two "PUMA-SA/330" aircraft from the Cannet-des-Maures (83) training base had conducted a night flight carrying out exercises (including ground lighting) in the area where the witnesses lived.

summary: Observations of a glow accompanied by noise.
description: On April 30, 1977, between 11:00 PM and 11:25 PM, witnesses saw a flash of light and heard a crackling or whistling sound. The police were notified of these events late and were unable to find any traces or clues at the scene. Witness accounts differ on many details, and the precise circumstances could not be established.

summary: Sightings of a dark, cigar-shaped object emitting a white light.
description: On April 29, 1977, at 9:15 PM and 10:15 PM, two people observed the slow movement of a cigar-shaped object. This object emitted lights of different colors and moved parallel to the Maine River. Despite a 10-minute observation, the witness accounts remained brief. A third witness, located by the gendarmerie, reported a three-minute observation that same day around 9:00 PM, describing the NE-SW movement of a red sphere with a "tail" that eventually "disappeared." The atmospheric reentry hypothesis was not confirmed due to a lack of information.

summary: Observation of a luminous phenomenon.
description: On April 2, 1977, between 7:15 and 7:30 PM, several people in a vehicle noticed a luminous cloud in the sky that intrigued them. The witnesses then saw an elongated glow that slowly detached from the cloud in a straight line. No unusual noise was heard by the witnesses, who had pulled over to the side of the road. The glow disappeared into a mass of cloud. No other accounts were collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Periodic observations of a glow. Slow movement.
description: On March 18, 19, and 20, 1977, several people, including police officers, observed a strange glow in the sky starting at 8:30 p.m. It moved slowly and appeared to grow larger or smaller at times. The color varied from white to orange-yellow. The glow disappeared around 9:00 p.m. The hypothesis of an astronomical observation could not be confirmed due to a lack of information.

summary: Observation of a bright object identified: optical effect of two lit torches.
description: On October 8, 1977, at 12:30 a.m., a driver and his passenger were startled by a luminous object that appeared to fly over their vehicle and land in a field at the roadside. The rounded craft was equipped with two nozzles that spit flames, illuminating the entire horizon. The witnesses were deeply shaken by their sighting. Following a police investigation, the witnesses admitted to having been misled by two lit torches that, depending on the wind direction, intermittently projected tall flames into the sky. These torches belonged to a gas station and were located on the edge of a field, the approximate location of the sighting.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of a luminous sphere.
description: On February 10, 1977, at approximately 5:58 a.m., two people observed from their homes the silent movement of a flashing luminous sphere. The sphere quickly disappeared to the north-northwest, hidden by the urban landscape. No other accounts of this phenomenon were ever collected.

summary: Observation of the movement of a luminous spherical shape.
description: On February 9, 1977, at approximately 6:50 PM, several people observed a strange glow in the sky, moving southeast along the mountain ridge. Initially stationary, this spherical glow gradually rose, changing color, and then suddenly disappeared. Contacted by telephone, the gendarmes at their station reported neither an unusual glow nor any unusual noise related to this phenomenon, about which we lack further information.

summary: Observations of a motionless and silent luminous phenomenon in the direction of the West: astronomical observations of Venus.
description: This case, classified as "C" by GEPAN, is currently under review (see the Investigation Notes document). On February 5, 1977, between 9:00 PM and 9:30 PM, two people in Reims (51) observed a luminous sphere in the west, seemingly motionless in the sky. No noise was heard during the observation of this phenomenon, which completely disappeared around 9:45 PM. While the case is somewhat sparse (two witnesses, but with brief accounts), the description of the observed UFO is quite precise. The sincerity and credibility of the witnesses have never been questioned. The described phenomenon shares many characteristics (duration of observation, shape, size, color) with a well-known astronomical object: the planet Venus. Furthermore, Venus was clearly visible in the observed area of the sky, with particularly remarkable brightness. It is not the visual perception of the witnesses that is the issue, but rather their interpretation of their observation based on their feelings (fatigue, nighttime observation). In the current GEIPAN classification, this case of weak strangeness is classified as A e, an observation linked to a misidentification of Venus.

summary: Observation of a luminous phenomenon.
description: On February 2, 1977, at approximately 8:45 PM, a witness observed a luminous phenomenon through binoculars for about three minutes. He described a circular shape in two parts: bright and yellow for the upper part and with a bright red flame on the lower part. The phenomenon then appeared to rotate on its axis, taking on an oval shape without any change in the intensity of the colors. The witness returned to his activities before the phenomenon disappeared. No other accounts have been collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Observation of the slow movement of a luminous phenomenon.
description: On the evening of January 27, 1977, starting at 8:30 p.m., two motorists observed the slow movement of a luminous phenomenon. A sphere the size of a football emitted a bright white light and moved silently while oscillating on its axis. The primary witness was unable to determine the distance or speed of the object, but also observed a second luminous point. The witness left the scene at 9:45 p.m. after the phenomenon had completely disappeared. No other accounts were collected regarding this phenomenon, for which we lack information.

summary: Observation of a dirigible-like shape.
description: On the last Wednesday of January 1977, a witness observed a flying object in the sky at an altitude of 500 meters from the first floor of a house. This object, shaped like a rugby ball, was large and resembled a blimp. It was moving at a speed of 100 to 150 km/h against the wind. Its color was a matte metallic gray. The witness heard no noise. This very late testimony (July 9, 2007) does not allow for a serious investigation that could validate or refute certain hypotheses, such as the passage of a balloon.

summary: Observation of an object falling into the ocean.
description: On January 24, 1977, at 6:17 a.m., three people saw a column of vapor or smoke rising from the sky. A patch of foam was visible on the surface, indicating that an object had fallen into the ocean approximately 4 km from the shore and about 8 to 10 km from the observation point. No other accounts of this phenomenon were collected, and as the impact point proved difficult to determine, no search was undertaken.

summary: Observation of the movement of luminous objects.
description: On January 23, 1977, at approximately 1:45 a.m., a witness observed an orange light in the distance that appeared to be coming from his direction. Awakening other people, these witnesses then saw luminous spheres very close together, each about the size of a football. One of the objects caught their attention because it was different from the others: rectangular in shape and narrower at the rear, with illuminated openings. These objects moved silently. The hypothesis that the object was a transport plane (given the presence of a military airfield in Châteauroux) could not be confirmed due to a lack of information.

summary: Observation of a lenticular cloud.
description: On January 17, 1977, around 5:00 PM, a motorist observed and photographed a peculiar meteorological phenomenon. An oval-shaped cloud was moving imperceptibly from north to south. Two other witnesses made the same observation. According to the photograph attached to the official report, these individuals saw a lenticular cloud.

summary: Observation of the movement of a luminous sphere.
description: On January 16, 1977, at 8:15 PM, a driver and his passenger observed the movement of a luminous orange sphere, approximately 15 cm in diameter. It was located at an altitude of about 2,000 meters. No trail or noise was visible during the observation. The object gradually faded three times before quickly reigniting. The object disappeared very rapidly.

summary: Observation of the movements of a luminous object.
description: On January 14, 1977, at approximately 6:40 PM, two people observed a spherical luminous object that intrigued them. This object initially moved in a south-south direction, then east-west. The gendarmes later noted the slow movement of a circular luminous object, larger than a star, in a westward direction. It remained visible until 9:30 PM. No further witness accounts were collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Observations of the passage of luminous phenomena.
description: On January 10, 1977, starting at 8:45 PM, several people in different departments observed unexplained luminous phenomena in the sky. They all described the silent and rapid movements of reddish, luminous objects. The police, called immediately, did not confirm these phenomena, about which we lack information.

summary: Observation of an object emitting a strong light.
description: On January 8, 1977, at 8:50 p.m., a witness observed an intense light emanating from an unseen object. No sound was heard during the brief observation. The object disappeared in a downward trajectory behind the houses, heading towards the state forest. No trace of the object and no other witness accounts have been found to provide further information regarding this phenomenon.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of a luminous phenomenon.
description: On January 5, 1977, at approximately 6:30 PM, two people in a car observed a red-orange luminous phenomenon that intrigued them. It appeared to originate from a mass moving southeast-northwest without any unusual noise being heard. The observation lasted about ten minutes, during which sparks were noticed. The phenomenon gradually and slowly diminished before disappearing completely. On several occasions, people traveling on the road taken by these motorists observed sparks coming from a power line oriented southeast-northwest. No other accounts were collected regarding this phenomenon, for which we lack information.

summary: Long observations of a stationary luminous object at low altitude; rapid and silent disappearance: observations of Venus.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, originally classified as A, B, C, or D, which are now being re-examined to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This observation, previously classified as D and named CHABEUIL (26) 01.01.1977, was first revisited in 2011. An accompanying star chart indicated the presence of Venus in the observed area of the sky. The new conclusion emphasizes the factors that contributed to the unusual nature of the case at the time and confirms the astronomical observation. On January 1, 1977, between 7:30 and 7:45 PM, two people were driving on a local road in the La Serre district of Valence (26). During their drive, they were intrigued by the presence of a very bright white light at a low altitude. Stationary and moving south, the large-shaped UFO then rose rapidly and disappeared, still heading south. No noise was heard during the long observation. A third witness, located by the police during the investigation, reported not having noticed anything unusual that evening or in his field, but described an observation of a UFO a year earlier. The observation is well-documented thanks to the photos and reconstructions made by the police. However, there are inconsistencies in the descriptions of the UFO's shape and movement. The near-stationary nature of the UFO over a significant period (two observations of at least 10 minutes separated by at least 15 minutes) suggests the observation of a celestial body. Regarding its appearance, certain witness accounts describing movement or a broad shape may have seemed strange and led to this hypothesis being dismissed during the initial investigation 40 years ago. However, the experience acquired by GEIPAN allows us to explain these perceptions. The variation in light intensity, caused by the evolution of the atmospheric veil in front of the object, is logically interpreted by the witness as a variation (called radial) in distance (in its direction) of a UFO that would have constant intensity and at speeds often described as lightning-fast, particularly during its flight and final disappearance. - Witness T1 says, "At that moment, the object moved at a dizzying speed towards the south"; Witness T2 said, "After about a minute, this craft began to rise and decrease in size. This maneuver lasted about five seconds, and at that moment, the fireball moved south like a shooting star. I should point out that this happened very quickly."... "I must add that when the craft took off, I had the impression that our car was rolling backward." It should be noted that the southward direction of movement is the same as that which the witnesses attribute to the direction of the UFO, which supports the perception of radial movement. Only T1 describes a movement that could suggest a non-radial trajectory with an evolution in position in the sky; he says, "it moved at a dizzying speed southward, describing a curve that started at about a 45° angle." T2 indicates a size larger than that of a celestial body, with projected shapes and radii. This also occurs during the confirmed observation of very bright celestial bodies such as Venus or Sirius near the horizon. The most common element (also attested to here) is the variable colors and flashing. It should be noted that the observation is made in the presence of, or near, patches of fog, which accentuate the dispersive effects of the atmosphere on the light emanating from the celestial body. Finally, it should be noted that T1 does not distinguish any shape beyond a large, generally round point of light, and that both witnesses often refer to a star when reporting the UFO. There is little room for doubt when one observes (see attached reconstruction based on police photographs) that Venus is almost exactly (within one or two degrees) in the direction of the UFO (234° and not due south as the witnesses believe). Venus did indeed follow a downward trajectory, reaching within a few degrees of the hilltop at the end of the observation. The intense brightness combined with the dispersion of light due to fog may have led observer T2 to believe the UFO was on the hill, at least since T1 consistently placed the UFO above ground. The UFO's eventual disappearance resulted from the passage of a thicker fog or cloud. The UFO's initial intelligence (at departure) in response to the presence of witnesses indicated by their headlights was purely coincidental; moreover, T2 specifies that the UFO's "reaction" took two minutes ("I have the impression that our car's headlights were a hindrance because two minutes after flashing the headlights, the craft left"). Venus is directly in the direction of the UFO. The deviations observed from the standard appearance of a star are consistent with those recorded during numerous confirmed observations of Venus or Sirius near the horizon, and what is not consistent (non-radial motion) is noted only by one witness (T1) and not by the other. In conclusion, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: observation of Venus.

summary: Observation of particular movements of a luminous phenomenon.
description: Recent testimony (July 12, 2009) of an earlier observation: during the summer of 1977 (the witness no longer remembers the exact date between June and August 1977), people observed a luminous object in the night sky. Initially stationary, it then moved at irregular speeds, changing direction. It then disappeared at high speed to the west. No other accounts of this phenomenon have been collected. Any investigation into this phenomenon today is difficult, if not impossible, due to a lack of information.
